newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA unit, gas plant trust in pipeline deal.
newsitem.headline: NOVA unit, gas plant trust in pipeline deal.

text.p: Nevis Ltd, a unit of the new Morrison Facilities Income Fund, said on Tuesday it signed a letter of intent with Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd to transport natural gas liquids to Boundary Lake, Alberta from Taylor in northeast British Columbia.

Under the deal, Nevis would convert an existing 40 km pipeline to natural gas liquids from crude oil. The converted line would transport volumes to the main NCL liquids pipeline proposed for Boundary Lake from a proposed liquids extraction plant at Taylor
NCL is a unit of NOVA Corp.

The move came on a busy day for Canada's hotly competitive gas liquids extraction and transportation business, where action involving several companies is centered in the northern regions of Alberta and B.C.

Federated Pipe Lines, co-owned by Anderson Exploration Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd, said earlier that its board gave the final go-ahead to proceed with a C$106 million expansion project that starts at Taylor and will ship liquids into Alberta.
NCL said the new deal gave momentum to its C$$235 million integrated liquids project planned for the region.
NCL and Nevis said its agreement required an amendment to a previous National Energy Board approval for NCL's proposed 58 km pipeline to Boundary Lake from Taylor.
The amendment would include replacing the middle section of pipe that NCL intended to construct with the existing Nevis pipeline, the firms said, adding the Nevis pipeline followed similar route.

"Our arrangement with Nevis allows us to advance our project while optimizing spare capacity on an existing pipeline," NCL vice-president Randy Findlay said in a statement. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
